summary: Built the val-pilot gate CORE LOGIC + FIXTURE SUITE (design step 2, read-only-scanner conception chosen by user over the executing-skill conception). scripts/automation/val_pilot_gate_lib.py = pure stdlib logic implementing design sections 2-5: verify_pilot (section 2 completeness + section 3 evidence rules, incl. metadata-missing/split=test/filename-metadata-disagreement/checkpoint-absent handling), is_stale (section 3 retrain-in-place hazard), match_command (section 4 exact checkpoint path+hash / run_name / seed / epsilon matching, non-match names the failing field), compute_verdict (section 5 STRONG-GO/REVIEW-GO/NO-GO/NEEDS-REVIEW with integrity-first precedence + dominance). scripts/automation/test_val_pilot_gate_cases.py = 31 fixtures covering design section 8 cases A-L plus verdict bands, dominance + strict-improvement counterexample, integrity override, and static safety meta-scan (no subprocess/network/eval/exec/--split in code; write-free except rb-hashing). ALL SYNTHETIC: temp-dir artifacts only, no real checkpoint, no real validation CSV, no held-out-test data, no --split command run, no results/ tree walked. Import audit confirms lib is pure stdlib (hashlib/dataclasses/pathlib/typing). 31/31 fixtures pass under both direct run and pytest. One fixture initially failed (safety scan flagged '--split' appearing in the lib's own prose describing what it must NEVER do); fixed by stripping comments+docstrings before the token scan, same spirit as the guard suite's permissionDecision-comment fix.
